Turn Maintenance Plans into Completed Work

Thematic Area: Asset Management & Maintenance Execution

How might we turn maintenance procedures and logbook records into assigned, scheduled and verifiable work across ships and machinery?

Background

A shipping and logistics group wants stronger execution of asset-maintenance work. Maintenance logbooks already exist, but adherence and follow-through remain weak.

The objective is to connect asset records and standard procedures with task ownership, due dates, completion evidence and overdue follow-up. Relevant startups offer asset-management systems, workflow software and mobile tools for completing and documenting planned work.

The collaboration will define an asset class, technical procedures and system connections with the operating team.

Significance of Problem

Key challenges include:

  • Missed maintenance: Unclear ownership and escalation leave scheduled tasks without effective follow-through.
  • Difficult completion checks: Supervisors need accessible evidence to review whether required work was completed correctly.
  • Operational disruption: Delayed attention to maintenance needs increases the risk of asset-related disruption.

Existing Efforts

  • Current company approach: Maintenance logbooks are already used. The priority is execution and adherence, linking records with practical follow-through.
  • Available capabilities: Configurable workflow software supports assignments, reminders, approvals and reporting. Road-fleet tools offer maintenance logs and servicing alerts for relevant vehicles.
  • Collaboration focus: Select an asset class, define responsibilities and implement the workflow from scheduling through completion evidence and supervisor review. Configure maritime, machinery and road-vehicle requirements for the assets included in the pilot.

Potential Market Size

  • Global enterprise asset management market: The global market was estimated in May 2025 at US$7.65 billion in 2024 and is forecast to reach US$19.68 billion by 2030, with 17.2% annual growth during 2025–2030. Asia Pacific is forecast to grow at 18.5% annually over that period. The market covers asset management across industries.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
